question.problem:
Given that the random variable $X$ has the probability density function

$$
f(x)={\begin{aligned}1-\frac{x}{2},\, & 0\le x\le 2 \\ 0,\, & \text{otherwise}\end{aligned}
$$

its cumulative distribution function is 

$$
F(x)={\begin{aligned}0,\, & x<0 \\ h(x),\, & 0\le x\le 2 \\ 1,\, & x>2\end{aligned}
$$

where $h(x)=${{field-1}}.
question.worked_solution:
Since our random variable $X$ has a probability distribution function $f(x)$ that is strictly positive only for $0\le x\le 2,$ the cumulative distribution function takes the following form:

$$
F(x)=P(X\le x)={\begin{aligned}0, & x<0 \\ {\int }_{0}^{x}f(t)\,\text{d}t, & 0\le x\le 2 \\ 1, & x>2\end{aligned}
$$

For the given probability density function, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{0}^{x}f(t)\,\text{d}t & ={\int }_{0}^{x}(1-\frac{t}{2})\,\text{d}t \\ \text{ } & ={(t-\frac{{t}^{2}}{4})|}_{0}^{x} \\  & =x-\frac{{x}^{2}}{4}.\end{aligned}
$$

So, the cumulative distribution function is given by

$$
F(x)={\begin{aligned}0, & x<0 \\ x-\frac{{x}^{2}}{4}, & 0\le x\le 2 \\ 1, & x>2.\end{aligned}
$$
